Notes on the back pond

The pond behind the barn is about forty feet across and three feet deep in the middle. Cattails grow along the north edge, and a fallen sweetgum log lies half in the water on the east side.

Green frogs and bullfrogs both live there. The bullfrogs call at night in June with a deep "jug-o-rum" sound; the green frogs sound like a loose banjo string being plucked.

In early spring, spring peepers sing from the woods before the pond warms up. They are tiny, about the size of a thumbnail, with a dark X on their backs.

The dogs are not allowed near the pond after dark, because Mara once chased a bullfrog into the water and came back covered in duckweed.

Tadpoles show up in late April. Most of them become frogs by August, but bullfrog tadpoles can take two years to change.
